title: Tau positron emission tomography results from TOGETHER, a double‐blind, placebo‐controlled Phase II study of bepranemab in prodromal–mild Alzheimer’s disease

one_line: The Phase II TOGETHER trial demonstrated that bepranemab, a mid-region tau-targeting antibody, slowed tau accumulation by 33–58% compared to placebo in patients with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease.
summary: The TOGETHER trial (NCT04867616) is a Phase II, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating bepranemab in patients with prodromal-to-mild Alzheimer's disease. Bepranemab is a humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody targeting a mid-region epitope of tau. Over an 80-week treatment period, 466 participants received either 45 mg/kg or 90 mg/kg of intravenous bepranemab or a placebo every four weeks. Efficacy was assessed via tau PET imaging at baseline, Week 56, and Week 80. Initial analyses of the full trial population revealed that bepranemab slowed tau accumulation by 33–58% relative to placebo in whole cortical gray and jack temporal meta regions at Week 80. The abstract concludes that bepranemab is the first antibody targeting the tau mid-region to slow tau accumulation and provide clinical benefit.

key_claims.claim: Bepranemab slows tau accumulation in the brains of patients with prodromal to mild Alzheimer's disease.
key_claims.evidence: Tau accumulation slowed by 33–58% versus placebo across both bepranemab arms (90 mg/kg and 45 mg/kg) in the whole cortical gray and jack temporal meta regions at Week 80.

methods.design: Phase II participant- and investigator-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled study
methods.population: Prodromal-mild Alzheimer's disease (aged 50-80 years), cerebral amyloid beta presence (PET or CSF), global CDR score of 0.5, CDR-Memory Box score ≥0.5

limitations: The abstract does not report explicit limitations.
Quantitative data for clinical outcomes are omitted entirely, with only biomarker (tau PET) outcomes presented to support the conclusion of clinical benefit.
red_flags: Spin between results and conclusion: The abstract's conclusion states that the therapy 'demonstrated a clinical benefit,' but the results section only provides evidence for a biomarker endpoint (tau accumulation via PET imaging), citing previously presented external data in the background instead of offering primary data here.

issues: The author byline and affiliations were entirely missing from the Markdown document.
